case_name: Dhirendra Pandey & Ors vs State Of Bihar & Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Dhirendra Pandey, Son of Late Ramchandra Pandey; Nilmani Pandey, wife of Dhirendra Pandey; Nivedita Pandey, daughter of Dhirendra Pandey (husband, wife, daughter)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Bihar; Shweta Prabhat, wife of Dr. Prashant Kumar (state, wife)

facts_of_case: Marriage was solemnized with the petitioner, Dr. Prashant Kumar, on 10.11.2012. It is alleged that she was being beaten up and abused after few days of her marriage.

legal_principles.principle: The ambit and scope of inherent power of the High Court under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. in quashing of the criminal proceeding in non-compoundable offences relating to matrimonial dispute is governed by settled law.
legal_principles.held: Recently discussed and adjudicated by a three-Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. vs. Babita Raghuvanshi & Anr. [(2013) 4 SCC 58].
cited_cases: Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. vs. Babita Raghuvanshi & Anr., (2013) 4 SCC 58

legal_principles.principle: In non-compoundable offences relating to matrimonial dispute, the court's inherent power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. can be exercised to quash the criminal proceeding.
legal_principles.held: Recently discussed and adjudicated by a three-Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. vs. Babita Raghuvanshi & Anr. [(2013) 4 SCC 58].
cited_cases: Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. vs. Babita Raghuvanshi & Anr., (2013) 4 SCC 58
